title: Modified SureSelectQXT Target Enrichment Protocol for Illumina Sequencing of FFPE Samples
author: Rosa-Rosa, Caniego-Casas, et al.

steps.title: Measure DNA integrity (DIN)
steps.instruction: Measure the DNA integrity number (DIN) for each FFPE DNA sample using the Agilent 2200 TapeStation (or equivalent).

steps.title: Fragment and adaptor‑tag DNA
steps.instruction: Select genomic DNA input amount (50 ng, 150 ng, or 500 ng) based on the sample’s DIN (e.g., use 50, 150, 500 ng for sample NT1 with DIN 6.4) and perform the SureSelect QXT “Fragment and adaptor‑tag the genomic DNA samples” step.

steps.title: Amplify adaptor‑tagged library
steps.instruction: Amplify the adaptor‑tagged DNA library using the standard SureSelect QXT amplification protocol (pre‑hybridization PCR, default 8 cycles unless otherwise modified).

steps.title: Assess library quantity and quality
steps.instruction: Quantify each amplified library and evaluate its size profile (e.g., Agilent 2200 TapeStation with D1000 ScreenTape) and record the concentration.

steps.title: Increase pre‑hyb PCR cycles for low‑DIN
steps.instruction: For low‑DIN samples (e.g., sample T1), increase the number of pre‑hybridization PCR cycles to 10 while keeping 50 ng input DNA and otherwise following standard library‑preparation conditions.

steps.title: Prepare library at half reagent volume
steps.instruction: Perform all library‑preparation reactions (fragmentation, adaptor tagging, amplification) using ½ × of the manufacturer‑recommended reagent volumes while maintaining 50 ng DNA input to increase DNA concentration.

steps.title: Set digestion time based on DIN
steps.instruction: For samples with DIN > 6, use 150 ng input DNA and a transposase digestion time of 30 min; for samples with lower DIN (≈4.6), retain the standard 50 ng input and 1 min digestion.

steps.title: Reduce post‑hyb PCR cycles to 10
steps.instruction: After hybridization, perform the post‑hybridization PCR with 10 cycles (instead of the default higher number) to limit PCR duplicates.

steps.title: Reduce probe amount and post‑hyb cycles
steps.instruction: Further modify the protocol by halving the amount of capture probes and decreasing the post‑hybridization PCR cycles to 8.

steps.title: Denature and dilute library pool
steps.instruction: If necessary, dilute the pooled library to 2 nM; then mix 5 µl of 2 nM library with 5 µl of 0.2 N NaOH, add 990 µl HT1 buffer to the 10 µl denatured mixture to obtain a final concentration of 10 pM.

steps.title: Prepare sequencing mix with reduced HT1
steps.instruction: Use a minimum of 600 µl HT1 buffer for the denatured pool, ensuring the final NaOH concentration does not exceed 0.0025 N and that the final library concentration is at least 8 pM.

steps.title: Calculate final library concentration
steps.instruction: Compute the theoretical final concentration using the formula Ci × Vi = Cf × Vf, where Ci is the initial pool concentration, Vi the initial volume, Cf the desired final concentration, and Vf the final volume (600 µl HT1 buffer).

steps.title: Adjust low‑concentration pool
steps.instruction: If the calculated final concentration (Cf) is lower than 8 pM, add 1 µl of 1 N NaOH to 9 µl of library pool, then add 600 µl HT1 buffer and re‑calculate; otherwise, proceed to sequencing.
